title: No ordinary decade
description: Bold silhouettes and fresh ideas take automotive design somewhere new.

cars.name: Lamborghini Countach LP400
cars.description: The original Countach LP400 turned the wedge-shaped dream car into a road-going reality. Its low nose, dramatic scissor doors and V12 mounted behind the cabin made it a defining supercar of the decade. The early LP400’s clean bodywork has a purity distinct from the wider, more heavily spoilered versions that followed.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent LP400 examples. Later LP400 S, 5000 and anniversary variants have different values.

cars.name: Ferrari 308 GTB Vetroresina
cars.description: Introduced in 1975, the 308 GTB paired Pininfarina’s compact sports-car shape with a transverse V8 behind the seats. The first cars used a glassfibre body, earning the Vetroresina name. Its flowing profile and open-gated manual gear lever helped define the character of Ferrari’s smaller mid-engined road cars.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP range around the consulted Vetroresina market guide’s roughly £125,000 median. Covers sound to excellent glassfibre GTBs; individual sales vary, and later steel-bodied GTBs are a different market.

cars.name: Porsche 928
cars.description: Porsche’s 928 offered a different vision of the sports car: a front-mounted V8, a spacious grand-touring cabin and a distinctive rounded body. Unveiled in 1977, it reached series production for the 1978 model year. Its rear-mounted transmission and individual styling made it a striking alternative to the familiar 911.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent early 4.5-litre 928 examples. Transmission, maintenance history and originality affect value; later S, S4 and GTS models are separate markets.

cars.name: Volkswagen Golf GTI Mk1
cars.description: The first Golf GTI helped make the practical hatchback an enthusiast’s car. Launched in 1976, it combined a light three-door body with a fuel-injected engine and sporting details. This 1979 example represents the original 1.6-litre generation, before later Mk1 updates and the larger 1.8-litre engine.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent 1.6-litre Mk1 GTI examples. Original early cars can command a premium; later 1.8-litre models, modified cars and cabriolets are separate markets.

cars.name: Datsun 240Z
cars.description: The 240Z brought a long bonnet, a fastback roofline and straight-six power to Datsun’s international sports-car range. Its combination of performance and everyday usability won a following well beyond Japan. The three-dial dashboard and opening rear hatch remain characteristic details of this early Z-car generation.

cost.basis: Rounded UK guide range for good to excellent standard 240Z examples. Rust condition, originality, steering configuration and restoration quality affect value; competition conversions are excluded.
